title: Agents reflect on the instructions and propose fixes
goal: Agents reflect at done on whether the instructions guided them, and each reflection becomes an instruction change or is dismissed.
details:
Reflection is part of the loop. When an agent closes a ticket, hug task done asks it one question: did the instructions (AGENTS.md section, tool descriptions, hug messages) guide you well, or did one mislead you or leave a gap? The answer is stored with the ticket as a Reflection note naming the exact instruction. hug task reflections collects open ones across the board, and a coordinator or Jørgen turns them into an instruction change (shown as a diff) or dismisses them.

Builds on tzc9hb (the loop in the AGENTS.md section) and x325pp (nudges only between tasks). done already prints a next line; the question goes there, and MCP task_done accepts an optional reflection field.

title: Contributions: agent feedback and GitHub intake with minimal bureaucracy
goal: Outside agents and people contribute to hug through one triage step, and we can always see who contributed what.
details:
Settle how outside agents and people contribute to hug with the least process: agent feedback, tickets written on forks, and GitHub issues all reach our board through one triage step, and we can always see who contributed what and what to pull.

Candidate design. Step 1: hug feedback "..." plus an MCP feedback tool opens a GitHub issue through the user's gh login, labelled agent-feedback, after a shown and confirmed preview. Step 2: hug task upstream ID on a fork opens a short issue linking that fork's hug/tasks ticket file. Triage, run by us: hug task inbox lists open issues (with linked fork tickets shown in full); take creates our ticket (author from issue or git author plus Model: line, link back), comments the board link and closes the issue; dismiss closes it with a reason. Two-way sync was considered and rejected: GitHub lacks our states, and untriaged items would pollute the board. Existing: huginn/internal/importer/github.go (gh issue list import), CONTRIBUTING.md contributor agreement, public repo with issues on. Option kept in reserve: a private channel (email or endpoint) if public issues leak or attract noise.
old_goal: Settle how outside agents and people contribute to hug with the least process: agent feedback, tickets written on forks, and GitHub issues all reach our board through one triage step, and we can always see who contributed what and what to pull.

title: The board keeps itself true: deduce what happened, ask when it can't
goal: Tickets match what really happened: hug writes what it can deduce from git and asks the owner what it cannot settle.
details:
Tickets match what really happened without a person reminding anyone. Two levels: (1) when hug can deduce an event with certainty from git or the board (a commit naming the ticket reached main, a release tag contains it, a branch recorded on take is merged), it writes that onto the ticket itself; (2) when it observes something it cannot settle (landed but checks unticked, a doing ticket with no activity, a commit on main naming no ticket, a merged branch whose ticket is still doing), it raises a clarification request on the ticket, addressed to its owner, who answers in place.

Children: deduce from git (wyvern), observations become questions (hatchling), one ticket in doing per agent (kestrel). Evidence for the ids: 58 of 179 main commits in 2 days end with (id). Related: 0hkaa5 background sync (fetch is where new main commits are seen), x1t1t1 (branch recorded on take), x325pp (nudges at a break), 3jtfw9 (answer in place), 6ephqk (stages, waiting_on, asked_by).

title: Requests: a person writes a request in a task, an agent turns it into edits
goal: A person writes a request on a task in their own words, and an agent turns it into ticket edits and closes it.
details:
In a task's detail, R opens a multi-line box where the viewer writes a request to the agents in their own words (short, dictated, rough). hug stores it on the task as an open request: who, when, the text verbatim. The task's owner, or whoever works the board, is told at once (recall hook and the write-command footer), reads it, turns it into systematic changes to the ticket (goal, checks, details, notes, state), and closes the request with a one-line account of what changed. The person sees open requests on the row ('req 1') and the account under the request in the detail.

Not the asked stage: that blocks the task on a person; a request is an open item for agents on any task in any state, and does not change its stage. Storage proposal (kestrel to confirm): a '## Requests' section, each request a block 'request by jhf 2026-11-17 23:52:' + indented text, closed by 'done by nautilus 23:58: set check 9's wording, added check 10'. CLI: hug task request ID - (stdin) | "text"; hug task requests (open ones, all tasks); hug task resolve ID N "what changed". MCP: task_update action request / resolve; task_list filter requests. Agent notice: boardcue gets kind 'request' (one line: 'Task board: jhf asks on 6ephqk: "..." Act on it, then: hug task resolve 6ephqk 1 "what changed"'), routed to the task's assignee, else to the coordinator. TUI: R in a detail (and on a list row); the overview shows a REQUESTS count in the header and the row marks 'req N'. Multi-line input shared with 41hhgn's answer box. title: Layout 3: every task file is ID.md and never renamed; rank and group in the file
goal: Every task file is .hug/tasks/ID.md for its whole life, with rank and group in the file, so links never break.
details:
Each task lives at .hug/tasks/ID.md for its whole life, so a path or URL to it never breaks (e.g. github.com/veridit/hug/blob/hug/tasks/6ephqk.md) and git log -- ID.md is its full history. The rank prefix, the slug and the group folder leave the file name: rank and group become front-matter fields. A move edits the moved task's rank: line; it never renames. The task's own folder stays .hug/tasks/ID/. Memories move to the matching branch name: muninn-notes becomes hug/memory (9taa9d check 2). hug upgrade migrates both, preview first.

Front matter, grouped: identity (id, title, type, priority, labels, group, parent, rank), state (state, stage, and the stage's object e.g. asked: {what, for, check, since, by} per 41hhgn), who and how (assignee, model, branch, worktree), time (created, updated, done_at, done_release). rank keeps today's string keys and re-spacing (ordering.go rankPlan), now as field edits; rebalance edits many files' rank: lines, never names. Order on read comes from the cache (one parse per file already). Group folders (later/, design/) become group: values. Slugs and old file names stay resolvable as refs (ids, prefixes, aliases already work), so old links in notes still find the task. Memory branch: hug/memory with .hug/memory/; muninn-notes is moved by hug upgrade and deleted after. Owner: wyvern (store, cache, sync) with kestrel (upgrade, import); hatchling for the memory branch. Seid and Statbus run their own hug upgrade.

title: Windows CI: a background syncer held the queue 30 s and no pass ran
goal: The Windows stall in TestBackgroundSyncBurstIsBatched is explained by the logs and fixed, with a test that fails first.
details:
When a test's settled() times out, the pass log and the failure say which lock each syncer waited on and for how long, and the cause of TestBackgroundSyncBurstIsBatched's stall on Windows (CI 44237364634) is found and fixed, with a counting test that fails first.

CI 44237364634 (a13d7c74), test-windows-cli: sync_test.go:223 'background pass still running after 30 s: queued true, busy true, pending false, turn held false'. Pass log: two passes at 04:31:24 and 04:31:28 (the task new), then none during the 20 notes or the 30 s after. queued true = a syncer past takeQueue (it holds the queue): in settle.wait (bounded by SettleMax 10 s) or in flock.Acquire(run). So a pass holding run did not end in ~90 s, while fetch/push have NetTimeout 60 s and log on timeout. takeQueue (mmm8c8, 4336e2b0) cannot spin: two TryAcquire and one Acquire(.probe), which a prober holds only across a non-blocking TryAcquire. Candidates (unmeasured): the pass at below-normal priority (b6jgpn, a201b2e6) starved by the parallel test load; local git without a deadline; deducePass. Earlier, different shapes: 44230245084 (pending true, ubuntu), 44156864971 (ubuntu). 8 of 8 local runs on macOS pass.

A person or agent marks a piece of a task's text with a comment, question or request that sits inline in the text, visible as text, with a recognizable sigil. The agent picks marks up, acts or answers, and resolves each by rewriting the ticket text to the clarified result and removing the mark. The dialogue that led there (the mark, replies, who and when) is appended to a history file attached to the task, never kept in the ticket.

Syntax (Jørgen 09:31-09:35Z, console): Seid things. A mark is a thing, space-dot-Capital, followed by its lowercase properties: .Request .by:jhf .at:2026-11-19T09:40Z .msg:"Can you shorten this?" Kinds: .Comment, .Question, .Request; replies are further things in the same run (.Answer .by:crab .at:... .msg:"..."). Properties: .by, .at, .msg, .on:"quoted words" (the span; without it, the sentence before the mark), .in:"NAME#line" or "NAME#section" (a pointer into an attachment). The run ends where prose resumes (a word without a leading dot). Span delimiters in the text (.( ... ).Request, .{ ... }.Comment) were considered and rejected by Jørgen 09:35Z: they break Markdown. Board scan 09:31Z: space-dot-Capital occurs 9 times in all task files (.Compiler 6, .Oject1, .Object2, .Feature), none a mark kind; lowercase dotfile paths (.hug, .md, .backlog) can never start a mark. History: each task's history.sdo in its folder (Jørgen 09:35Z), hug's own Open-data variant (.sdo, Jørgen 11:07Z; Seid's Open tier is unfinished) (.Uppercase constructors, .lowercase properties, seq ... end), append-only; on resolve the agent rewrites the text and appends .Resolved .at:... .was:"..." .now:"..." .marks: seq <the run> end. Also set aside: CriticMarkup (wraps prose in brackets), bare inline properties (a property needs a thing). Replaces ## Questions and ## Requests over time (q2adr8, hbgybn); open marks show in ASKED and requests as those do now; delivery as gmzd87. TUI: a mark mode in the detail view selects a span; c comment, ? question, r request; open marks drawn calmly (qh9ep1 check 9), a key jumps between them. Anchors by structure (Jørgen 09:44Z): .prev:.Sentence means the sentence just before the mark, with no quote to go stale; likewise .prev:.Word, .prev:.Paragraph, .prev:.Item (a list item or check). .on:"quoted words" stays for a span inside it. With neither, the mark means .prev:.Sentence. Example: Make it concise. .Request .by:jhf .prev:.Sentence .msg:"Make it concise" Parsing rule (Jørgen 10:22Z): a constructor as a value stands alone. In .prev:.Sentence .msg:"..." the .msg belongs to the mark, not to .Sentence. A value with its own properties is parenthesized: .prev:(.Sentence .n:2) means the second sentence back. The giveaway (Jørgen 10:23Z): ':.' followed by a capital letter is a constructor value (.prev:.Sentence); ' .' (space-dot) followed by a capital letter starts a new thing in the run (.Request, .Answer). A scanner needs only those two cases. Ending rule (Jørgen 10:24Z): everything that continues a run starts with a dot (a property .x:, a value :. or a thing ' .Capital'); the first token that starts any other way ends the run, and prose resumes. Hard-to-quote text (quotes, several lines) goes in a triple-quoted string: .msg:"""he wrote "true" here
and on a second line""". The opener is """ and the closer is the first """ not followed by another quote, so a closing quote inside the text may touch the delimiter (""""). Seid's SYNTAX.md has no triple-quoted string yet (rg '"""' found none, 10:25Z); this is hug's rule until Seid defines one. Rulings on the mock (crab 10:31Z, from MOCK.md into the ticket 11:35Z): mark numbers are display only, in text order; CLI --on is the span (.on), --near WORDS finds the unit; resolve needs --now TEXT or --keep; .Resolved keeps .by .field .check .msg; an .in: mark sits at the end of ## Notes; hug writes marks verbatim, no escaping. Not Seid-parsable, by design (Jørgen 11:37Z): Seid quotes text inside code with {{ ... }} (design/Kernel-Seid.md section 2b); a ticket is the inverse, Markdown text with data blended in, and the marks are acted on, then removed. So the mark grammar is hug's own, defined here; a whole ticket is never fed to Seid. history.sdo is pure data and may follow Seid's Open tier once it exists. Name (Jørgen 11:37Z): SeidDataMarkdown, Markdown where data is a piece of the text itself. The mark grammar in these details is its first definition; hug owns it until Seid takes it up. Edits are the notification (Jørgen 11:47Z): when hug tui gets back from the editor on a task file or one of its files (editFiles, files.go:141-158; editorMsg, tui.go:1330), it already re-lints and commits; it then diffs that commit, and if the diff adds text (new marks, or any added lines in an attachment) it delivers to the assignee or coordinator as a request does (gmzd87), naming the task, the file and the commit, so the agent reads the diff. Edits outside hug: on the next hug command's sync, a new open mark found by the scanner is delivered the same way.

title: Agent instructions: questions in tickets, no blocked to quiet a reminder

title: Prototype: recall memories delivered into the dialogue by harness notify
goal: A per-harness prototype delivers recalled memories into the dialogue by the harness's notify path, measured against today's.
details:
A prototype, switchable per harness, delivers recalled memories straight into the agent's dialogue by the harness's own notify path (jcode notify_session, as hug task delivery gmzd87 does), instead of parking them for the first tool call. Measured against the current path; if it works it replaces it on harnesses that support it, with the hook path as the fallback where notify is not available.

Step 1 (evidence, no code): from capture/hook logs and injections, count for the last 3 days how many turns had a recall block parked and dropped by turn_end (no tool call), against delivered; and whether a soft-interrupt message (pasted mid-turn) runs turn_start recall at all. Step 2: prototype on jcode: on turn_start recall, deliver the block by notify_session to the same session (deliver.go), flag in config, default off. Step 3: per-harness availability table: jcode (notify_session socket), Claude Code and Codex (UserPromptSubmit additionalContext already lands before the answer, so nothing to do?), others. Related: z9q42h (park), gmzd87 (deliver.go), memory 5kxgm9. Step 2 scope (crab 19:05Z, from STEP1.md): normal turns already get their block (404/436 on 11-18, 100/107 on 11-19); the loss is messages typed mid-turn (soft interrupts): 0 of 123 got recall, and 8 of 13 stale drops come from a paste overtaking the park. Step 2 builds, behind config recall.jcode_midturn (default off): on post_tool_feedback, if the session journal holds user messages newer than the parked turn's message and not yet recalled, recall each and deliver its block in that tool result, never dropping the parked block as stale because of a paste (deliver both). No new daemon; idle sessions never woken for a memory alone. Plus logging: injections.delivered_at (or a delivered table), a hook.log line when a park is overwritten, session id on hook timeout lines. When jcode adds a soft-interrupt hook (maintainer asked 14:30Z), switch to it.

title: hug tui left running does not pick up new releases
goal: A hug tui left open across a brew upgrade notices the new binary and reloads, so nobody works on an old version.
details:
A hug tui left open across a brew upgrade notices the new binary and offers or does a reload, so a person never works for days on an old version.

title: Releases group their tickets and carry the owner's feedback questions
goal: Each release is one ticket that groups what it ships and asks the owner, one question each, whether it works for him.
details:
A ticket closes when its work ships; its checks hold only what the worker can prove (tests, CI, goldens). Each release is one ticket: the parent of every ticket it contains, linked by hug when the tag is cut, and the place where the owner is asked, one question each, whether the shipped changes work for him. It stays asked until he has answered, then is done. A no becomes a new bug linked to the original ticket and the release; the original stays closed.

Pieces: (1) hug task deduce / release step sets --parent RELEASE on each ticket a new tag contains (release ticket found or created by title 'Release vX.Y.Z'); hug task ls --epic RELEASE lists them; TUI shows the children under a release. (2) Owner-confirm checks: help, AGENTS.md section and worker instructions say they go on the release ticket as asks, not on the ticket. (3) lint: shipped-not-done does not fire on release tickets; its fix names moving the check to the release ticket. (4) Migration for the 40 shipped doing tasks: move each open 'Jørgen confirms' check to an ask on its release ticket, strike it on the task with a pointer, done the task if nothing else is open. (5) crab's release procedure from v0.7.82: release ticket gets its children and one ask per shipped change. Related: gpyqq9 (ask settles shipped-not-done), deduce.go:101-153, q2adr8 (several questions).
